newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 24.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 24.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Tuesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- The truth commission postponed hearings into the amnesty applications of Clive Derby-Lewis and Janusz Walus, the killers of South African Communist Party leader Chris Hani.

- Delays in implementing the government's teacher redeployment strategy would cost all provincial education departments about 47 million rand per month, Education Minister Sibusiso Bengu said in a court application.
- Hopes for a merger of JCI and Lonrho were dampened after Lonrho chief executive Nick Morrell said talks were at a preliminary stage.
- The Johannesburg Stock Exchange all gold index slumped to its lowest level since March 1993 as bullion's near four-year low again bulldozed sentiment on Tuesday.

- A power struggle between the National Union of Mineworkers and a rival group, the Workers' Mouthpiece, was believed to be behind the death of a NUM shopsteward at Rustenburg Platinum Mine, police said.

- The government, police, traffic officials and the African National Congress condemned plans to block roads across the country to protest against rampant crime, but organisers said the blockade would go ahead.

- The African-American investors who backed Pepsi's abortive return to South Africa are looking for ways to revive the venture after the struggling soft drink firm pulled the plug on bottler New Age Beverages last month.
BUSINESS REPORT
- Mauritian police arrested the Johannesburg-based organiser of a Sub-Saharan Oil and Minerals Conference at the weekend, charging him with conspiring to obtain credit fraudulently.

- British Airways would not make an offer for South African Airways SAA.CN if there were South African shareholders who "might affect the running of the airline", British Airways director Robin Renwick said.
- Only 60 percent of the 248,000 houses the government claimed were built or were under construction since it took power in 1994 are actually completed houses, sources said.

- Cosatu said it would support the amalgamation of the South African Clothing and Textile Workers' Union and the National Union of Leatherworkers, the two largest labour voices in the footwear and leather industries.

- A Johannesburg-based consortium, which is launching a new equity investment fund focusing on the Western Cape, has acquired a controlling stake in Cape clothing and knitwear company Towles, Edgar Jacobs (Tej), the consortium said.
THE STAR

- The killers of Chris Hani said in their written amnesty applications to the Truth and Reconciliation Commission they had acted alone, but believed they had the backing of the Conservative Party when they assassinated the Communist Party leader.
- Police in France have issues a warning for people to beware of fierce 80 kg close-combat killer dogs imported from South Africa, known as boerbuls.
SAKE-BEELD
- The Johannesburg Stock Exchange is introducing new measures to combat price manipulation, executive president Russell Loubser said.
- Transnet's PX parcel delivery services has been thrown into chaos with the restructuring of its labour force.
- The liquidators of Supreme Holdings are going ahead with legal steps to demand 100 million rand from the country's larest financial institutions.
- Iscor is in talks with trade unions about job losses resulting from the conversion of its Pretoria plant from a stainless steel facility into a carbon steel plant.
